public.explanation: Makes a class, method, constructor, or field accessible from anywhere that can see the declaring package/module.

private.explanation: Makes a member accessible only inside the same class.

protected.explanation: Makes a member accessible inside the same package and from subclasses.

abstract.explanation: Marks a class that cannot be instantiated directly, or a method that has no body and must be implemented by a subclass.

final.explanation: Prevents reassignment for variables, overriding for methods, or inheritance for classes.

static.explanation: Marks a member as belonging to the class itself instead of to a specific object instance.

strictfp.explanation: Obsolete keyword that used to require strict floating-point behavior; modern Java already evaluates floating-point expressions strictly.

synchronized.explanation: Allows only one thread at a time to execute a method or block using the same monitor lock.

transient.explanation: Marks a field so it is skipped by Java object serialization.

volatile.explanation: Marks a field so reads and writes go directly to main memory, helping visibility between threads.

native.explanation: Declares that a method is implemented in platform-specific native code, not in Java.

class.explanation: Defines a blueprint for creating objects with fields, methods, constructors, and nested types.

interface.explanation: Defines a contract of methods/constants that classes can implement; modern interfaces may also contain default and static methods.

enum.explanation: Defines a fixed set of named constants as a special class type.

package.explanation: Places a source file's classes inside a named package for organization and name disambiguation.

import.explanation: Brings a type or static member into scope so it can be used without its fully qualified name.
import.example:
import java.util.ArrayList;

ArrayList<String> names = new ArrayList<>();

extends.explanation: Declares that a class inherits from another class, or that an interface extends another interface.

implements.explanation: Declares that a class provides the methods required by one or more interfaces.

this.explanation: Refers to the current object instance, often used to distinguish fields from parameters.

super.explanation: Refers to the parent class, commonly used to call a parent constructor or overridden method.

new.explanation: Creates a new object or array instance.
new.example:
Point p = new Point();
int[] nums = new int[3];

instanceof.explanation: Tests whether an object is compatible with a type; also supports pattern variables in modern Java.

if.explanation: Runs a block only when a condition is true.

else.explanation: Runs an alternative block when the preceding if condition is false.

switch.explanation: Selects a branch based on a matching value or pattern; can be used as a statement or expression.

case.explanation: Defines a branch inside a switch statement or switch expression.

default.explanation: Defines the fallback branch in a switch, or a default method implementation in an interface.

for.explanation: Repeats code using a traditional counter loop or an enhanced for loop over arrays/collections.

while.explanation: Repeats code while a condition remains true, checking the condition before each iteration.

do.explanation: Starts a do-while loop, which runs the body once before checking the condition.

break.explanation: Immediately exits the nearest loop or switch.

continue.explanation: Skips the rest of the current loop iteration and moves to the next one.

return.explanation: Exits a method and optionally sends a value back to the caller.

try.explanation: Starts a block of code whose exceptions can be caught or whose resources can be automatically closed.

catch.explanation: Handles an exception thrown inside a matching try block.

finally.explanation: Runs cleanup code after try/catch, whether or not an exception occurred.

throws.explanation: Declares that a method may throw one or more checked exceptions.

assert.explanation: Checks an assumption during debugging and throws AssertionError if the condition is false when assertions are enabled.

boolean.explanation: Primitive type that stores either true or false.

int.explanation: 32-bit signed integer primitive type, commonly used for whole numbers.

long.explanation: 64-bit signed integer primitive type for large whole numbers.

float.explanation: 32-bit floating-point primitive type; literals usually use the f suffix.

double.explanation: 64-bit floating-point primitive type, commonly used for decimal calculations.

char.explanation: 16-bit UTF-16 code unit used to store a single character.

void.explanation: Used as a method return type to show that the method does not return a value.

const.explanation: Reserved for possible future use; Java does not use it for constants. Use final instead.

goto.explanation: Reserved but not used by Java; included so compilers can give better errors.
goto.example: // goto is reserved but not supported in Java

_.explanation: The single underscore is reserved and cannot be used as a normal identifier; in some contexts it can mark an unnamed variable/pattern.

true.explanation: Boolean literal representing a true condition.

false.explanation: Boolean literal representing a false condition.

null.explanation: Reference literal representing the absence of an object.

module.explanation: Declares a Java module in module-info.java.

open.explanation: Marks a module as open, allowing reflective access to all its packages.

opens.explanation: In a module declaration, opens a package for deep reflection, optionally to specific modules.

exports.explanation: In a module declaration, exports a package so other modules can access its public types.

requires.explanation: In a module declaration, declares a dependency on another module.

transitive.explanation: Used with requires to re-export a required module to modules that depend on this module.

uses.explanation: In a module declaration, declares that the module consumes a service.

provides.explanation: In a module declaration, declares a service implementation supplied by the module.

to.explanation: Used in module directives such as exports ... to or opens ... to to target specific modules.

with.explanation: Used in a provides directive to name the implementation class for a service.

var.explanation: Lets the compiler infer a local variable or lambda parameter type from the initializer.
var.example:
var count = 0;
var names = new ArrayList<String>();

yield.explanation: Returns a value from a switch expression block.

record.explanation: Declares a compact data carrier class with generated constructor, accessors, equals, hashCode, and toString.
record.example:
record Point(int x, int y) {}
Point p = new Point(3, 4);

sealed.explanation: Restricts which classes or interfaces may extend or implement a type.
sealed.example: sealed class Shape permits Circle, Square {}

non-sealed.explanation: Reopens inheritance for a subclass of a sealed class or interface.

permits.explanation: Lists the specific classes or interfaces allowed to extend or implement a sealed type.
permits.example: sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Square {}

when.explanation: Adds a guard condition to a pattern case in switch pattern matching.

main.explanation: Conventional application entry method name used by the JVM to start many Java programs.

String[] args.explanation: Common parameter for command-line arguments passed to the main method.

for-each.explanation: Informal name for Java's enhanced for loop over arrays or Iterable collections.

enhanced for.explanation: Official-style term for the for loop form that iterates directly over arrays or Iterable values.

do-while.explanation: Loop pattern using do and while where the body runs at least once.

try-with-resources.explanation: try form that automatically closes resources implementing AutoCloseable.

lambda expression.explanation: Creates an anonymous function-like implementation of a functional interface.

method reference.explanation: Short syntax for passing an existing method as a functional interface implementation.

generics.explanation: The <T> syntax lets classes, interfaces, and methods work with specific types while preserving compile-time type safety.

diamond operator.explanation: The <> syntax lets Java infer generic type arguments during object creation.

annotation.explanation: Metadata attached to code elements using @ syntax.

array.explanation: Fixed-size indexed container whose elements all have the same type.

java.base.explanation: The fundamental Java module that contains core packages such as java.lang, java.util, java.io, java.nio, and java.time.

java.lang.explanation: Fundamental package automatically imported into every Java source file; includes Object, String, System, Math, wrapper classes, and exceptions.

java.util.explanation: Utility package containing the collections framework, Optional, Scanner, Random, properties, and other common utility classes.

java.io.explanation: Classic input/output package for streams, readers, writers, files, and IOException.

java.nio.explanation: New I/O package for buffers, channels, charsets, and scalable I/O operations.

java.nio.file.explanation: Modern file-system package with Path, Files, and file walking/copying utilities.

java.time.explanation: Modern date and time API package including LocalDate, LocalDateTime, Instant, and Duration.

java.math.explanation: Package for arbitrary-precision numeric classes such as BigInteger and BigDecimal.
java.math.example:
import java.math.BigDecimal;
BigDecimal price = new BigDecimal("19.99");

java.net.explanation: Networking package for URLs, URIs, sockets, and network-related classes.

java.util.concurrent.explanation: Concurrency utilities such as ExecutorService, Future, locks, and thread-safe collections.

java.util.function.explanation: Functional interfaces used by lambdas and method references, such as Function, Predicate, Consumer, and Supplier.

java.util.stream.explanation: Stream API package for processing sequences of data with map/filter/reduce-style operations.

java.util.regex.explanation: Regular expression package with Pattern and Matcher.

java.sql.explanation: JDBC database API package for Connection, Statement, ResultSet, and SQL exceptions.

javax.swing.explanation: Classic desktop GUI toolkit package for windows, buttons, labels, and other UI components.

Object.explanation: Root superclass of all Java classes.

Class.explanation: Runtime representation of a class or interface.

String.explanation: Immutable sequence of characters used for text.

StringBuilder.explanation: Mutable sequence of characters, useful for efficiently building strings.

System.explanation: Provides standard input/output/error streams, current time, environment access, array copy, and system utilities.

Math.explanation: Provides common mathematical functions and constants.

StrictMath.explanation: Provides reproducible math functions with strict results across platforms.

Enum.explanation: Common base class of all enum types.

Throwable.explanation: Superclass of all objects that can be thrown and caught.

Exception.explanation: Base class for checked exceptions that applications may catch or declare.

RuntimeException.explanation: Base class for unchecked exceptions that usually indicate programming/runtime errors.

Error.explanation: Base class for serious JVM or system-level problems that applications usually should not catch.

Thread.example:
Thread t = new Thread(() -> System.out.println("Running"));
t.start();

Runnable.explanation: Functional interface representing code that can run without returning a value.

Comparable.explanation: Interface for objects that define their natural ordering.

Iterable.explanation: Interface for objects that can be used in an enhanced for loop.

AutoCloseable.explanation: Interface for resources that can be closed automatically by try-with-resources.

Cloneable.explanation: Marker interface indicating that Object.clone may make a field-for-field copy.

Number.explanation: Abstract superclass of numeric wrapper classes like Integer, Long, Float, and Double.

Boolean.explanation: Wrapper class for the primitive boolean type.

Byte.explanation: Wrapper class for the primitive byte type.

Short.explanation: Wrapper class for the primitive short type.

Integer.explanation: Wrapper class for the primitive int type.

Long.explanation: Wrapper class for the primitive long type.

Float.explanation: Wrapper class for the primitive float type.

Double.explanation: Wrapper class for the primitive double type.

Character.explanation: Wrapper class for the primitive char type.

Void.explanation: Non-instantiable class representing the void type in reflection.

Collection.explanation: Root interface for many container types such as List, Set, and Queue.

List.explanation: Ordered collection that allows indexed access and usually allows duplicates.

LinkedList.explanation: Doubly-linked list implementation of List and Deque.

Set.explanation: Collection that does not contain duplicate elements.

HashSet.explanation: Hash-table implementation of Set with fast lookup and no guaranteed order.

TreeSet.explanation: Sorted Set implementation based on a tree.

Map.explanation: Associates keys with values; each key maps to at most one value.

HashMap.explanation: Hash-table implementation of Map with fast key lookup and no guaranteed order.
HashMap.example:
HashMap<String, Integer> ages = new HashMap<>();
ages.put("Nina", 37);

TreeMap.explanation: Sorted Map implementation based on keys' natural order or a Comparator.

Queue.explanation: Collection designed for holding elements before processing, often FIFO.

Deque.explanation: Double-ended queue that supports adding/removing from both ends.

ArrayDeque.explanation: Resizable-array implementation of Deque, often used as a stack or queue.

Collections.explanation: Utility class with static methods for sorting, searching, synchronizing, and creating collection views.

Arrays.explanation: Utility class with static methods for arrays, such as sort, binarySearch, fill, and asList.

Optional.explanation: Container object that may or may not hold a non-null value.

Scanner.explanation: Parses text input from strings, files, or streams.
Scanner.example:
Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
String line = scanner.nextLine();

Random.example:
Random random = new Random();
int n = random.nextInt(10);

Properties.explanation: Hashtable-based class commonly used for configuration key/value pairs.

Comparator.explanation: Compares two objects to define custom ordering.

Stream.explanation: Represents a sequence of elements that can be processed with operations like map, filter, and reduce.

Predicate.explanation: Functional interface representing a boolean test of one value.

Function.explanation: Functional interface representing a transformation from one value to another.

Consumer.explanation: Functional interface representing an operation that accepts a value and returns nothing.

Supplier.explanation: Functional interface representing a provider of values.

LocalDate.explanation: Date without time-of-day or time zone.

LocalDateTime.explanation: Date and time without a time zone.

Instant.explanation: A point on the UTC time-line.

Duration.explanation: Time-based amount, such as 5 minutes or 2 hours.

Period.explanation: Date-based amount, such as 3 days or 2 months.

BigInteger.explanation: Arbitrary-precision integer class for whole numbers larger than long can hold.

BigDecimal.explanation: Arbitrary-precision decimal class, commonly used for money and exact decimal arithmetic.

File.explanation: Legacy file and directory pathname class from java.io.

Path.explanation: Modern representation of a file-system path.

Files.explanation: Utility class for reading, writing, copying, moving, and walking files using Path.

InputStream.explanation: Base class for reading bytes from a source.

OutputStream.explanation: Base class for writing bytes to a destination.

Reader.explanation: Base class for reading character streams.

Writer.explanation: Base class for writing character streams.

BufferedReader.explanation: Reads text efficiently by buffering characters from another Reader.

IllegalArgumentException.explanation: Unchecked exception thrown when a method receives an invalid argument.

NullPointerException.explanation: Unchecked exception thrown when code tries to use null as if it were an object.
NullPointerException.example:
String s = null;
// s.length(); // would throw NullPointerException

IndexOutOfBoundsException.explanation: Unchecked exception for invalid index access.

ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.explanation: Unchecked exception for invalid array index access.
ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.example:
int[] nums = {1};
// nums[2]; // would throw this

NumberFormatException.explanation: Unchecked exception thrown when parsing a number from invalid text.

ClassCastException.explanation: Unchecked exception thrown when an object is cast to an incompatible type.

InterruptedException.explanation: Checked exception thrown when a waiting/sleeping thread is interrupted.
InterruptedException.example: Thread.sleep(1000); // must handle or declare InterruptedException

ArithmeticException.explanation: Unchecked exception for arithmetic errors such as integer division by zero.

AssertionError.explanation: Error thrown when an assert statement fails while assertions are enabled.

@Override.explanation: Tells the compiler that a method is intended to override a superclass or interface method.

@Deprecated.explanation: Marks an API element as discouraged for use, often because it will be removed or replaced.

@SuppressWarnings.explanation: Suppresses selected compiler warnings for the annotated element.

@FunctionalInterface.explanation: Marks an interface as intended to have exactly one abstract method.

@SafeVarargs.explanation: Suppresses heap-pollution warnings for safe generic varargs methods or constructors.

Connection.explanation: JDBC interface representing a database connection.

DriverManager.explanation: JDBC utility class for obtaining database connections.

PreparedStatement.explanation: Precompiled SQL statement that safely accepts parameters.
PreparedStatement.example: PreparedStatement ps = conn.prepareStatement("select * from users where id = ?");

ResultSet.explanation: Represents rows returned from a database query.

SQLException.explanation: Checked exception for JDBC/database access errors.

ExecutorService.explanation: Manages and executes asynchronous tasks using a pool of worker threads.

Executors.explanation: Factory utility class for creating ExecutorService instances.

Future.explanation: Represents the result of an asynchronous computation that may complete later.

CompletableFuture.explanation: Future implementation that supports chaining asynchronous operations.

==.explanation: Compares two values. For objects - INCLUDING Strings - this asks whether they are the same object in memory, not whether they look the same. Use .equals() to compare text.

!=.explanation: "Is not equal to". For objects this compares identity, like == does.

%.explanation: Remainder (modulo): what is left over after division. n % 2 == 0 means n is even.

/.explanation: Division. Between two INTEGERS this throws away the remainder: 7 / 2 is 3, not 3.5. Make one side a double to get a decimal.

++.explanation: Adds one to a variable, in place.

+=.explanation: Adds to a variable and stores the result back in it.

&&.explanation: Logical AND: true only when both sides are true. Stops at the first false side, so the right side is not even evaluated.

||.explanation: Logical OR: true when either side is true.

=.explanation: Assignment: puts the value on the right into the variable on the left. To COMPARE use == .
